chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Habbar narrated from Ali ibn al-Sindi, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Ibn Udhaynah, from Zurarah and al-Fadl ibn Yasar, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:

When the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) was taken on the Night Journey and reached the Bait al-Ma'mur, the time for prayer arrived. Gabriel (peace be upon him) called the Adhan and then the Iqamah. The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) stepped forward, and the angels and prophets formed rows behind him.

We asked him, 'How did he call the Adhan?' He said: 'Allah is the Greatest, Allah is the Greatest. I bear witness that there is no god but Allah. I bear witness that there is no god but Allah. I bear witness that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah. I bear witness that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah. Come to prayer, come to prayer. Come to success, come to success. Come to the best of deeds, come to the best of deeds. Allah is the Greatest, Allah is the Greatest. There is no god but Allah, there is no god but Allah.'

The Iqamah is the same as the Adhan, except that in it, 'Qad qamat al-salah' (Prayer has risen) is said twice, placed between 'Come to the best of deeds' and 'Allah is the Greatest, Allah is the Greatest'.

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) ordered Bilal to call the Adhan with this format, and he continued to do so until Allah took (passed away) His Messenger (peace be upon him and his family).

key_terms.الْبَيْتَ الْمَعْمُورَ: The Bait al-Ma'mur, a celestial house in heaven visited during the Night Journey
key_terms.بِلاَلًا: Bilal, the companion known for his voice, who was ordered to call the Adhan
key_terms.جَبْرَئِيلُ: Gabriel, the archangel who called the Adhan
key_terms.حَيَّ عَلَى خَيْرِ الْعَمَلِ: Come to the best of deeds, a phrase included in the Adhan in this narration
key_terms.قَدْ قَامَتِ الصَّلَاةُ: Prayer has risen, a phrase inserted into the Iqamah in this specific format

ai.seo_question: What is the specific format of the Adhan and Iqamah described in the Night Journey hadith from Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: This hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) describes the Adhan and Iqamah as they were called during the Prophet's Night Journey (Isra) in the presence of angels and prophets. It establishes a specific format for the Adhan that includes 'Hayya 'ala khayr al-'amal' (Come to the best of deeds) and details the placement of 'Qad qamat al-salah' in the Iqamah, noting that Bilal continued to use this format until the Prophet's passing. Scholarly tradition highlights this as evidence for the authenticity of 'hayya 'ala khayr al-'amal' in the Adhan, distinguishing it from the Sunni practice which often omits it, thereby affirming the completeness of the prophetic call to prayer as preserved in Shia jurisprudence.
